newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures underperformed their German counterparts on Thursday as concerns about France's ability to hit public deficit targets in 1997 and talk of an early election unsettled nervous traders.
The gap between French and German 10-year bonds narrowed five basis points to minus eight while June PIBOR slumped, lagging the equivalent Euromark contract by 10 basis points.
Traders said persistant rumours that there would be a dissolution of parliament, dismissed by Chirac's office on Wednesday, were circulating.

A report in French afternoon daily Le Monde, which said an internal report suggested the public deficit could be as high as 3.8 percent of GDP in 1997, compounded the initial jitters, traders and analysts said.

"I think it's more the news about fiscal prospects (hitting bonds) but it is true also markets would not like a dissolution," Eric Chaney at Morgan Stanley in Paris said. "It would really move markets as it would create such uncertainty."
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis responded to the speculation by issuing a statement saying France would take the necessary steps hit the three percent target.
Both the June PIBOR and bond future climbed from their closing levels on GLOBEX trade following the Arthuis statement.

Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance, said he thought the concerns about the deficit overshoot and a dissolution of parliament were overdone although they had affected the market today.
"It was a combination of the deficit, which I think is a bit silly and politics, which is also a bit silly, the odds are they would lose much of their majority," Brossard said.
Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais was equally sceptical about the likelihood of an early election.

"I still go with the idea a reshuffle is not a bad idea, but dissolving parliament is complete hogwash. It's political suicide. They might scrape a majority, but why lose the handsome one they have?" Lindsay said.
Traders said there had been switching out of French bonds into Bund futures because of the various concerns. French notes and bonds underperformed the length of the curve.

June PIBOR was hit by a wave of selling, notably by US funds, pushing the daily volume to its highest level since August 22, 1996. Out of a total of 73,716 lots, one US fund was said to have sold 26,000 alone.
Still, the French Treasury managed to sell 24 billion francs of BTANs earlier on Thursday, at the top of its expected range, keeping the heavy pace of funding so far this year on track.
The franc weakened slightly against the mark, trading at 3.3657 compared with 3.3621, although traders said the volume had been relatively light.
One trader at a French bank quipped that the Bank of France would probably be relieved, having bought so many marks to stop the franc appreciating during the past couple of weeks.
As expected the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent at a regular money market tender.
